proposals: Nigeria’s Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority should publish monthly refinery-by-refinery output alongside product imports and exports, so Dangote’s 57 per cent share of fuel supply and Nigeria’s reported net-exporter status rest on regulator data rather than trade-press reporting.

Nigeria’s National Bureau of Statistics should publish monthly refined-product exports by product and destination, so claims such as 466,000 tonnes of jet fuel shipped to Europe in a single month can be checked against official customs records.

The Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority should publish a status register of Nigeria’s 24 planned refinery projects, with licence stage, capacity and target date, so progress toward 2.64 million barrels a day by 2031 can be tracked against an industry with a record of multi-year slippage.

The African Energy Chamber should publish the list of refinery projects and capacities assumed in its 2050 outlook, plus a 2024 product-level import baseline, so readers can tell whether the 3.4 million barrels-a-day import forecast already counts Nigeria’s new pipeline and Dangote’s 1.4 million expansion.
